last_transition_reason: The proof matches the stated lemma and cleanly derives the quotient formula by expanding the Gaussian q-binomial definitions, substituting n-a=r+b and n-b=r+a, factoring the relevant q-Pochhammer symbols, reindexing the tail product, and cancelling common factors. The hypotheses 0 <= a <= b and a+b <= n are used exactly to ensure all q-Pochhammer indices are nonnegative and the interval products are well-formed. No forbidden or undeclared dependencies are used.
latest_nl_proof:
Work in the field of rational functions in q, so that all displayed divisions are legitimate formal operations. Since 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, the number r := n - a - b is a nonnegative integer, and
n - a = r + b,    n - b = r + a.
Hence all q-Pochhammer symbols that appear below have nonnegative indices.

By the stated definition of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient,
([n choose b]_q)/([n choose a]_q)
= ((q;q)_n / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{n-b})) / ((q;q)_n / ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{n-a}))
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{n-a}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{n-b})
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{r+b}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{r+a}).

Now use the definition (q;q)_m = product_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j) together with the empty-product convention. Because a <= b,
(q;q)_b = (product_{j=1}^a (1 - q^j)) (product_{j=a+1}^b (1 - q^j))
= (q;q)_a * product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^i).
Similarly,
(q;q)_{r+b} = (product_{j=1}^{r+a} (1 - q^j)) (product_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j))
= (q;q)_{r+a} * product_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j).
Reindex the last product by j = r + i. As i runs from a+1 to b, j runs from r+a+1 to r+b, so
product_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j) = product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i)).
Therefore,
(q;q)_{r+b} = (q;q)_{r+a} * product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i)).

Substituting these two factorizations into the earlier expression gives
([n choose b]_q)/([n choose a]_q)
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{r+a} * product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i))) / (((q;q)_a * product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^i)) (q;q)_{r+a})
= (product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i))) / (product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^i))
= product_{i=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)).

If a = b, each product from i = a+1 to b is empty, hence equal to 1, and the same computation yields 1 on both sides. Thus the claimed identity holds for all integers n, a, b with 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n.
role_in_parent: Rewrites the reduced Gaussian quotient as the canonical shifted interval q-factorial ratio P_{a,b,r}(q).
statement_nl: For integers n, a, b with 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, define r := n - a - b. Then the quotient of Gaussian q-binomial coefficients satisfies [n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q = product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), where [n choose t]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_t (q;q)_{n-t}), (q;q)_m := product_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j), (q;q)_0 := 1, and an empty product is interpreted as 1.

domain_restrictions: r is forced to be n minus a minus b, hence r is nonnegative under the stated hypotheses
The variable q is not given an explicit domain; the expressions require a context where powers, finite products, and division make sense
The definition of [n choose t]_q presumes t and n minus t are appropriate integers for the q Pochhammer factors
The definition of (q;q)_m uses nonnegative integers m
The product over i from a + 1 to b is empty exactly when a = b, and then it equals 1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every triple of integers n, a, b satisfying 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, if r is defined as n minus a minus b, then the quotient of the Gaussian q binomial coefficient of n choose b by the Gaussian q binomial coefficient of n choose a equals the finite product from i = a + 1 to b of (1 minus q to the power r plus i) divided by (1 minus q to the power i), with the convention that an empty product equals 1 and with the q binomial and q Pochhammer symbols defined by the stated finite products.
quantifier_order: For all integers n, a, b with 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n
Define r as n minus a minus b
For the stated formula, q is an implicit parameter with no explicit domain specified
For each integer t with 0 <= t <= n, define [n choose t]_q by the given q Pochhammer quotient
For each nonnegative integer m, define (q;q)_m by the given finite product, with (q;q)_0 equal to 1
For the product over i from a + 1 to b, multiply the stated factors, using the empty product convention when a = b
For the product over j from 1 to m, multiply the stated factors in the q Pochhammer definition
